players.product: GPU cloud / AI compute capacity (NVIDIA GB300 NVL72)

quarterly_data.signal: ChronoScale's 10-K (fiscal year ended May 31, 2026): revenue $71,604 thousand, down 15% from $84,376 thousand; cost of revenues $88,691 thousand; operating loss $37,497 thousand; net loss $50,320 thousand. The Cloud Business (formerly Applied Digital Cloud) was about 99.5% of revenue; it rents space at third-party colocation centers in Colorado, Minnesota and Utah and runs company-owned GPU equipment, with additional deployable capacity at each site to be offered as GPU-as-a-Service and through its Token Factory managed inference offering; it also offers ChronoScale Foundry, an enterprise agentic-AI platform. Purchase obligations for AI infrastructure were $3,757 thousand at May 31, 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue $71,604 thousand (-15%); net loss $50,320 thousand; Cloud about 99.5% of revenue

quarterly_data.signal: ChronoScale's 10-K customer concentration: one customer accounted for 100% of fiscal 2026 revenue (fiscal year ended May 31, 2026), versus Customer A 77% and Customer B 23% in fiscal 2025; the company expects one or a limited number of customers to continue to account for a high percentage of its revenue for the foreseeable future.
quarterly_data.figure: one customer 100% of FY2026 revenue; FY2025 Customer A 77%, Customer B 23%

quarterly_data.signal: ChronoScale's 10-K corporate structure: on May 5, 2026 Ekso Bionics Holdings combined with Applied Digital Cloud Corporation in a reverse acquisition (renamed ChronoScale), after which Applied Digital and its subsidiary held approximately 97% of the common stock and legacy Ekso holders about 3%. A holding company, ChronoScale Holdings, became the listed parent on July 1, 2026, and the board committed on May 29, 2026 to divest the Legacy Ekso exoskeleton business (held for sale).
quarterly_data.figure: Applied Digital approximately 97% ownership after the May 5, 2026 combination

quarterly_data.signal: ChronoScale's 10-K: in August 2026 ChronoScale announced a strategic partnership with Nutanix, Inc. to jointly deliver enterprise AI infrastructure - extending Nutanix on-premises environments into ChronoScale GPU-as-a-Service capacity, Token Factory prepaid inference and ChronoScale Foundry - with joint go-to-market, solution development and technical integration, to be implemented through one or more definitive agreements.

connects_to.relationship: 50-MW AI compute deployment on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems

contracts.signal: ChronoScale's 10-K: on August 6, 2026 ChronoScale entered a two-year GPU services agreement (strategic partnership) with Microsoft for a planned deployment of approximately 50 megawatts of AI compute capacity on NVIDIA GB300 systems with liquid cooling at a dedicated data center facility, with projected completion in the first calendar quarter of 2027; GPU capacity is delivered in tranches on a fixed schedule with daily delay credits, tranche or contract termination rights and refunds of upfront payments, and the deployment depends on ChronoScale obtaining financing.

players.product: NVLink Switch, B200 GPU, GB200 superchip

connects_to.relationship: NVIDIA GPUs (H100 clusters; GB300 NVL72 for the Microsoft deployment) for ChronoScale's GPU cloud

contracts.signal: ChronoScale's 10-K: it currently relies on Nvidia (and plans to rely on AMD) for the GPU chips it offers customers; its H100 clusters are NVIDIA GPUs, and the Microsoft deployment relies on a sole-source GPU supplier for NVIDIA GB300 clusters.
